newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech 39-wk T-bill auction yield avg. 12.20 pct.
newsitem.headline: Czech 39-wk T-bill auction yield avg. 12.20 pct.

text.p: The average yield in an auction of 39-week Czech treasury bills was 12.20 percent and the offer of five billion crowns was oversubscribed with bids totalling 8.55 billion, the Czech National Bank said on Wednesday.
It said the minimum accepted bid was 12.14 percent and the maximum accepted bid was 12.26 percent in the American-style auction.
The 1995 state budget revenues reached 439.9 billion crowns, while expenditures were 432.7 billion.
The Czech centre-right government has made a balanced state budget a cornerstone of its anti-inflationary policy.
It has proposed a draft of the country's fifth straight balanced budget to the parliament, which is scheduled to start debating it later during its current October session.
The cabinet agreed on 9.3 billion spending cuts in August in order to balance budget by the end of this year, after it slipped into deficit partly due to lower-than expected tax revenues.
The 1996 budget showed a 48 million crown surplus at the end of September, with revenues standing at 347.392 billion and expenditures at 347.344 billion.
